title: Data Center Backlash Unites Americans Across Party Lines in Rare Bipartisan Revolt
excerpt: From conservative rural Utah to liberal California, opposition to AI data centers has become one of the few issues uniting Democrats and Republicans, with 70% of Americans opposing local construction as New York halts new projects.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • 70% of Americans oppose local data center construction, uniting Democrats and Republicans against projects.
  • Over 800 grassroots groups are active against 1,500 planned data centers across 49 states.
  • New York halted data center construction on July 14, becoming the first state to do so.
  • Rising electricity costs and distrust of tech companies fuel opposition to data centers nationwide.
  • India is aggressively attracting data center investments, contrasting with American community pushback.

  • Seventy percent of Americans oppose local data center construction, with backlash crossing party lines — 75% of Democrats and 63% of Republicans are against projects in their area, according to Gallup.
  • At least 75 data center projects worth roughly $130 billion were stalled or blocked in Q1 2026, with more than 800 opposition groups active across 49 states.
  • New York became the first state to halt data center construction on July 14; President Trump blasted the moratorium as "terrible" and defended data centers as "money machines."
  • As America pushes back, India is aggressively courting data center investment, raising questions about whether similar resource concerns will follow.

A Rare Bipartisan Consensus

In one of the most politically divided countries on earth, Americans have found something they can agree on: they do not want AI data centers in their backyards.

https://x.com/Alexer38/status/2078523251719029089

A June Reuters/Ipsos poll found that only 14% of Americans would support a data center in their community. According to Gallup, 75% of Democrats and 63% of Republicans oppose local data center development. Yale Program on Climate Change Communication data reveals a striking detail: 53% of conservative Republicans oppose data centers, versus 44% of moderate Republicans — placing staunch conservatives closer to liberal Democrats than to their own party's centrists.

"I'm not sure I've ever seen a chart where conservative Republicans are closer to liberal Democrats than liberal and moderate Republicans are," said Anthony Leiserowitz, the Yale program's director.

More than 800 grassroots groups are now active across 49 states opposing some 1,500 planned data centers. In Q1 2026, at least 75 projects worth approximately $130 billion were stalled or blocked, according to NBC News.

"In Box Elder County, Utah — where Trump won nearly 80% of the vote in 2024 — a 40,000-acre project faces intense opposition over its impact on the drying Great Salt Lake."

From Town Halls to the Campaign Trail

In Saline Township, Michigan — a farming community of 2,400 — a $16 billion Stargate data center backed by Oracle, OpenAI, and Blackstone is under construction despite fierce opposition. The township board voted 4-1 to deny rezoning but was sued by developers and forced into a settlement allowing construction with $14 million in community benefits.

"We really just didn't think it was fair that our board got forced into this position."

— Tammie Bruneau, Saline community activist

The issue is reshaping Michigan's Democratic Senate primary ahead of August 4. Representative Haley Stevens is running as a tech optimist, while rival Abdul El-Sayed has called for local moratoriums and greater oversight of AI companies.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed an executive order on July 14 imposing a one-year pause on new data center construction — the first state-level halt in the country. President Trump responded the next day, calling it "terrible" and describing data centers as "one of the biggest Driving Forces in the Future for Jobs," according to USA Today.

The backlash extends into Republican territory. Texas Governor Greg Abbott has unveiled recommendations to rein in data center development. In Box Elder County, Utah — where Trump won nearly 80% of the vote in 2024 — a 40,000-acre project faces intense opposition over its impact on the drying Great Salt Lake. In Monterey Park, California, voters permanently banned data centers by ballot measure.

Impact of Data Center Opposition
›75 data center projects worth $130 billion stalled in Q1 2026.
›800+ opposition groups active across 49 states.
›New York's moratorium is the first of its kind.
›Communities cite rising costs and environmental concerns.

What Is Driving the Anger

The grievances are consistent across the political spectrum: rising electricity bills, water scarcity, noise, loss of farmland, and distrust of tech companies. Just 7% of voters trust tech CEOs to make decisions affecting their lives, according to Tech Oversight. Rising living costs, amplified by the conflict with Iran, have made communities sensitive to anything threatening higher utility bills.

"It seems like the big tech companies are kind of steamrolling the citizens," Jeff Samoray, a 57-year-old Democrat from outside Detroit, told Reuters.

India Rolls Out the Red Carpet

As American communities push back, India is moving in the opposite direction. State governments are competing for hyperscale data center investments, with Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru emerging as major hubs. Tax breaks, data localization rules, and relaxed environmental standards are accelerating approvals — often without the public hearings that have become flashpoints in the US.

For the Indian diaspora, the contrast is stark. NRIs in the US tech sector are building AI infrastructure their American neighbors oppose, while India courts the same facilities with few of the safeguards communities are demanding stateside. Analysts warn that similar water and energy concerns could eventually surface in India as well.

What Comes Next

Whether the bipartisan backlash holds through the midterms is uncertain. The anti-fracking movement followed a similar arc — broad early support that eventually fractured along party lines.

India's Data Center Investment Surge
›India is competing for hyperscale data center investments.
›Major hubs include Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru.
›Tax breaks and relaxed standards accelerate approvals.

"This feels to me like the early days of the fracking fight," Alex Beauchamp, northern regional director at Food and Water Watch, told Grist. "A lot of Republicans were really up in arms about it in the beginning, and then it slowly became a partisan issue."

Senator Bernie Sanders has sponsored a bill calling for a national moratorium, while the White House is working on a voluntary pledge to protect taxpayers from AI expansion costs, according to Reuters. With midterms approaching in November, data centers are poised to become a defining local issue — one where the usual political playbook does not yet apply.
